title: Multilevel and Sequential Monte Carlo for Training-Free Diffusion Guidance
claim: Posterior over clean data is multimodal at high noise, so point estimates fall in low-density regions and give biased guidance.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, contour plots with shared axes and marker overlays
description: Two side-by-side 2-D contour plots, labeled (a) t=900 and (b) t=600, with axes x1 and x2 from -4 to 4. Both show a Gaussian mixture posterior in blue shades, where darker blue means higher density. In (a), eight Gaussian blobs form a ring with an empty center. A red dot and a black X sit in the empty center, away from any mode, and a green star marks a target mode on the right. In (b), the posterior has narrowed to about three blobs in the upper right. The red dot now lies near a mode, and the black X sits between modes. The eye goes first to the ring of blue blobs, then to the markers. The figure shows that a point estimate can fall in low-density gaps between modes at high noise.
caption: Posterior $p(x_0\mid x_t)$ for an 8-component ring GMM. Panels show high noise ($t=900$, left) and moderate noise ($t=600$, right).
abstract: We address the problem of accurate, training-free guidance for conditional generation in trained diffusion models. Existing methods typically rely on point-estimates to approximate the posterior score, often resulting in biased approximations that fail to capture multimodality inherent to the reverse process of diffusion models. We propose a sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) framework that integrates over the full denoising distribution to construct an unbiased Monte Carlo estimator of $p_Î¸(y\mid x_t)$, avoiding the bias of existing training-free guidance methods. To ensure computational tractability, we incorporate variance-reduction schemes based on MultiLevel Monte Carlo (MLMC). We evaluate on three image generation tasks. On CIFAR-10 and ImageNet classifier guidance, our approach improves accuracy by 18 and 38 points respectively over the strongest training-free baseline. On CelebA-HQ joint-attribute guidance, three existing methods (DPS, LGD, TFG) used within our framework all outperform the closest SMC-based comparator (TDS) by 25-37 points, and improve over the strongest baseline by 2-14 points.
